layout_pattern: 20 slides, all classified as generic 'content' (no distinct title/TOC/closing detected by shape-count heuristics) — but titles themselves reveal structure: opens with a cover slide, then a repeated section-divider title ('企业互联迈入5G+SD-WAN时代') recurs 3 times (slides 1, 5, 17), each time introducing a new sub-section. So the real pattern is: cover -> [divider + N content slides] x3 -> case study close. Section dividers are marked by a short repeated title phrase, not by a distinct layout.

color_role_mapping.1D1D1A: primary text color, most frequent (77) — near-black rather than pure black
color_role_mapping.C00000: accent/emphasis red (57) — third most frequent, consistent with the other two samples

typography_hierarchy.usage: most frequent size overall (65) — appears to be the dominant body/label size

data_viz_preference.note: no native pptx charts or tables at all — heavy reliance on images (12/20 slides have pictures), meaning data visualization likely happens as embedded screenshots/graphics rather than editable chart objects. This is a meaningfully different pattern from the Telefonica deck (which used native tables heavily).

text_density_rule: Wide variance: 14-370 characters per slide (mean ~163). Cover and section-divider slides are short (14-45 characters); content slides that carry a full argument run 150-370 characters. No fixed cap — density tracks whether a slide is a divider vs a substantive content slide.
logic_flow: Headline-as-title throughout: nearly every slide's title is a full declarative sentence stating the slide's conclusion (e.g. '技术积累带来好的市场表现，良好市场表现反哺技术创新'), not a topic label. Overall arc: business/tech drivers -> Huawei's accumulated capability -> three technical highlights (with sub-proof points) -> customer case study close. This is the 'headline = conclusion' McKinsey-style pattern.
image_treatment: 44 images across 20 slides (~2.2/slide), spread across every zone with a heavy middle-center cluster (10) and secondary weight toward middle/bottom-right and bottom-left — consistent with a diagram-heavy deck where graphics sit beside or below argument text rather than as full-page hero shots (only 2 of 44 are full-bleed). 11 of 44 (25%) carry an adjacent label (e.g. '云化\n2020年，85%企业业务上云' beneath an icon) — icon+short-label pairing, not editorial captions.
citation_style: Zero citation markers detected anywhere in this deck. Every figure and claim (technical benchmarks, market stats) appears uncited — contrasts with the Telefonica deck, which cites at least its headline external figure.
argument_structure: Substantive slides carry a median of 18 content points (range 4-30), fairly flat rather than bimodal — consistent with a pitch deck where each slide develops one point at similar depth, no sharp split between navigation and explanation slides the way the BLM deck shows.
diagram_convention: 16 of 20 slides (80% — the highest rate in the corpus) have ≥3 non-text diagram shapes forming a 2D grid arrangement, e.g. slide 2 ('商业驱动：更多的企业在转型过程中对网络提出更高诉求', 15 shapes, ~4x6) and slide 4 (17 shapes, ~6x5) — consistent with icon/capability walls illustrating market drivers. No single-row or single-column sequence diagrams found — no evidence of funnel/timeline-style conventions.
branding_footer: No footer, page-number, or confidentiality marker found anywhere in this sample.
data_quality_caveats: layout_type classifier produced only 'content' for every slide here — the shape-count/char-count heuristic doesn't distinguish cover/divider/case-study slides in this deck; title_text (from the actual title placeholder) is what actually reveals structure. Treat layout_pattern above as derived from title text, not from the layout_type field.
